transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-13 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samir Patel, Claire Huang (Redwood); Dr. Lena Ortiz, Marcus Bell, Priya Nair (Polarbyte)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching strategy and KV/prefix prefetch economics for Polarbyte's long-session multi-turn assistant. Ran a couple of simulated scenarios in the sandbox cost model, discussed tradeoffs between latency SLOs and token unit cost, and agreed on pilot to validate prefix cache hit assumptions.

Topics covered:
- Baseline: current traffic profile and session length distribution
- Batching windows and latency budgets
- Prefix / KV prefetch heuristics and memory sizing
- Cost model assumptions (per-token, per-GPU-hour, cache miss penalties)
- Security & deployment constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2)
- Pilot plan and next steps

Action items (captured in metadata) and links:
- Cost-model spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/sandbox/polarbyte/cost-model (sample link)
- Sandbox Optimize studio: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/polarbyte (invite to follow)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: All right uh thanks everyone for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is Claire from our Solutions Engineering team. Quick intro?
[00:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Hey Samir, thanks — i'm Lena, CTO at Polarbyte, we've been evaluating a hybrid route — some hosted endpoints but most inference on reserved infra for cost reasons.
[00:21] Marcus Bell: Marcus here, SRE, i'll be configuring nets and peering for sandbox.
[00:26] Priya Nair: Priya, ML eng, i own the sessionization and prompt templates.
[00:31] Claire: Great, thanks. Today we'll run through Optimize's batching & KV prefetch recommendations, then look at a couple of econ sims for your traffic. We'll call out configs that target <150ms P95 and also cost-first profiles.
[00:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Our target is P95 under 200ms for short flows, but for longer conversations we tolerate up to 400ms if it cuts cost. We mainly care about unit cost per 1k sessions.
[00:58] Samir: Perfect, that's helpful. Priya, can you remind us of your median session length and tokens?
[01:05] Priya: Median is about 14 turns, average prompt+response tokens per turn ~220, session length distribution is heavy tail — 60% under 10 turns, 20% between 10-30, 5% above 70.
[01:20] Claire: Excellent — that tail is where prefix KV prefetch shines. I'll pull up the sandbox sim we prepared.
[01:28] [02:05] Claire: (screen share) So here's the baseline: single-request routing to hosted LLM, no prefetch, batch size effectively 1 because requests are bursty; cost per 1k sessions in this baseline is ~$120 (note: numbers high-level) — in the spreadsheet it's $0.00034 per token, compute hours accounted for, and we included expected latency penalty on cache-miss path. Sorry possibly mis-typed there as $0.0003 per tunk in the sheet.
[02:40] Marcus: That baseline lines up with what we measured internally, good. Show us the prefetch scenario.
[02:47] Claire: OK switching to Prefetch A — prefix/KV prefetch at turn 2 using a 64-token lookahead prefix and aggressive batching (window 20ms or until 8 requests). This yields a simulated cache hit of ~42% under your trace assumption and reduces per-1k session cost to ~$78 in sim. Latency P95 stays near 170ms.
[03:20] Priya: How sensitive is the hit rate to small changes in prompt wording? Our prompts include dynamic metadata (customer name, product IDs).
[03:30] Claire: Good question, prefix strategy scopes to canonicalized prefix only — Optimize supports a normalization hook to strip volatile tokens before generating prefix hashes. That pushes hit rates up. In our sim we applied a normalization function but the real-world gain will depend on cleanups you can do server-side.
[03:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Also worried about memory — if we prefetch many session prefixes do we need more KV memory or bigger SSD backing?
[04:00] Claire: You'll see the memory projection in the sheet — at 42% hit with your traffic we estimated ~48 GB of resident KV working set, plus SSD fallback enrichment for less-frequent prefixes. We include cost for extra memory in the calc.
[04:18] Samir: And we can show a dedicated variant with quantized models that further drop per-token compute cost — trade is sometimes slight lat increase on first token.
[04:30] [05:10] Claire: Now batching: we tested a concurrency-aware batching policy that holds up to 12ms micro-window and will batch up to 16 requests, while using session-affinity for bursty users. For your traffic this reduces per-token compute overhead by about 18% because of amortized kernel launch and KV lookups.
[05:50] Marcus: If we push batch sizes higher will we break your latency SLO?
[05:56] Claire: There's a tradeoff — beyond 20-30ms batching window, P95 starts to climb. Our recommending sweet spot given your 200ms target is 10-25ms depending on burstiness. Optimize can simulate several windows quickly.
[06:15] Priya: The spreadsheet shows a case with session-cache instead of prefix prefetch; can you explain differences?
[06:23] Claire: Sure — session cache stores full KV cache per active session so hits are high for repeated conversation, but memory cost is higher and eviction churn matters; prefix prefetch tries to load likely next-KV keys before the next token generation and is cheaper memory-wise for predictable dialogue patterns. For your workload, prefix prefetch wins on cost for sessions under ~30 turns; session cache helps for the tiny percent of ultra-long sessions.
[06:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We also operate in EU-only region, data residency is important. How does the sandbox reflect region and KMS?
[07:00] Samir: We can run the same sim in our eu-west region and wire up customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. We'll attach our SOC2 + KMS notes after the call.
[07:11] [07:45] Claire: Back to the cost model — here's the simulated run for a canary: two configs, Config A (balanced latency/cost) does prefetch + 12ms batch window, projected savings ~35% vs baseline. Config B (cost-first) uses heavier batching, more quantization, and reduces cost ~55% but P95 is closer to 320ms.
[08:12] Marcus: If we need deterministic tail latency, can we run dedicated pooled GPUs with reserved capacity?
[08:18] Samir: Yes, Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail variance. Our calc models dedicated pricing in a separate tab; often it's a small up-front commit but lowers unit cost for high sustained throughput.
[08:30] Priya: Can we run the pilot on a few reserved nodes but route a portion of traffic to hosted fallback? We want graceful degration if capacity spikes.
[08:40] Claire: Absolutely — Optimize supports routing policies and automated fallback to compatible model variants in hosted tier. We'll capture a routing policy example in the pilot runbook.
[09:00] [09:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On the security front we need audit logs, RBAC, and long-term trace redaction — does Redwood provide that in Private or Dedicated?
[09:40] Samir: Yes, Dedicated and Private can ship extended audit retention and integrate with your SIEM. Private gives you full control over logs. We'll share the docs.
[09:54] Priya: Back to KV prefetch heuristics — what heuristics do you use to pick which keys to prefetch?
[10:02] Claire: We use a heatmap from session traces: next-token n-gram frequency, turn-position heuristics, and metadata signals (user type, intent tag). Optimize's console surfaces a ranked list of candidate prefixes and estimated marginal benefit per prefetch.
[10:22] Marcus: The console simulation shows a marginal savings chart that flattens after 3 lookahead slots — is there a cost to lookahead too far?
[10:30] Claire: Yes exponential cost of storing more KV entries and increased prefetch SSD reads. In most cases 1-3 lookahead steps capture most of the savings. For you, 2-step lookahead was the knee.
[10:50] [11:25] Priya: Do you support TTLs or adaptive evictions for prefixes? We rotate a lot of ephemeral data.
[11:33] Claire: TTLs, LRU, and a weighted frequency eviction are supported. We can also wire up custom eviction rules if you have privacy constraints to drop PII-related prefixes sooner.
[11:50] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Show us the pilot matrices; what metrics will you collect?
[11:58] Claire: We'll capture: cache hit rate, P95 latency, tokens per session, per-1k-session cost, GPU utilization, and error rates. All surfaced in the console.
[12:10] [12:45] Samir: Quick demo of the Optimize studio: here you can toggle batch window and prefix lookahead and the cost model recalculates live. Note — spreadsheet and console may differ slightly because console includes GPU queueing overhead and real kernel perf we've profiled.
[13:05] Priya: I noticed the console estimated per-token compute cost a bit lower than the spreadsheet — can you reconcile those?
[13:12] Claire: The console uses profiler-derived kernel timings for the specific model family we simulated, the spreadsheet uses a conservative flat per-token cost. We'll align them in the pilot by using your traces to derive a custom profile.
[13:32] [14:00] Marcus: Regarding network egress for VPC peering, does prefetch increase outbound bandwidth significantly?
[14:06] Claire: Prefetch results in upstream calls to fetch KV blobs but those are typically intra-cluster or SSD reads — egress overhead is minor unless you prefetch huge context objects. We still account for it in the econ tab.
[14:25] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Can we do an experiment that compares 1) no prefetch + small batch; 2) prefetch + small batch; 3) large batch + no prefetch — just to isolate effect?
[14:36] Claire: Yes that's exactly the A/B we propose for the pilot. We'll also try a 4th arm with session cache to validate tail cases.
[14:48] [15:10] Samir: One practical note: for normalization and prefix hashing we'll need a short client library change (two lines to call the canonicalizer) — Priya, is that workable?
[15:20] Priya: Yeah we can do that, minor change in our request pipeline. Should be fine.
[15:27] Marcus: What's the rollback plan if pilot increases error rates?
[15:31] Claire: We recommend feature flags on the prefetch path, metric-based gates (error rate > 0.5% or P95 > 400ms) to auto-disable prefetch, and fallback to hosted variant. We'll include those gates in the runbook.
[15:43] [16:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Any privacy issues with storing prefixes that contain user data?
[16:07] Claire: We support PII scrubbing hooks before prefix generation, auto-redaction rules, and TTLs. If you require, we can run the KV store inside your VPC with keys wrapped by your KMS — that'll satisfy most compliance requests.
[16:25] Priya: About quantization — your sheet includes a Q4/INT8 simulation. Does that affect prefix correctness?
[16:32] Claire: Quantization affects model logits and sometimes slight changes in token generation ordering, but prefix hits are by string/canonicalized prefix so not impacted. However generation divergence can change hit probability downstream, so we account for that in sensitivity sims.
[16:54] [17:30] Claire: I'll run a quick live sim: feeding your sample trace (Priya's traces) into the sandbox. Running... (pause) OK results: baseline per-1k-sessions $124 -> prefetch config drops to $79 -> combined prefetch+quant gives $62 in-sim. Hit rate observed on these traces ~46% with normalization.
[17:58] Priya: That delta is compelling. Is the simulator repeatable across time windows? We see varying traffic by day.
[18:05] Claire: The simulator lets you seed different trace windows; we'll run weekend vs weekday samples in the pilot.
[18:20] [19:00] Samir: I'll recap the recommended pilot: 10k sessions over 7 days, 4 arms (baseline, prefetch A, large-batch no-prefetch, session-cache), metrics collected and dashboarded. Claire will own runbook, we'll provide sandbox + cost spreadsheet.
[19:20] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Timing — we want pilot started by July 20th if possible.
[19:26] Samir: We'll aim to get invites and artifacts over Friday the 17th and kick off the pilot 20th.
[19:34] [20:05] Marcus: One more question — do you provide libraries for canonicalization and prefetch client, or do we build in-house?
[20:12] Claire: We have a small client helper (open source-ish) that does canonicalization and exposes a prefix-only mode. We'll share the repo link.
[20:20] Priya: Great. Also can the console flag sessions for manual inspection when a prefetch misses badly?
[20:28] Claire: Yes — console lets you drill into missed prefixes, replay trace, and annotate. Useful for prompt engineering loops.
[20:40] [21:15] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Cost allocation question — for internal chargebacks can we break out cost by team/route?
[21:22] Samir: Yes the Console supports per-route cost breakdown and token-level attribution. We'll show an example in the next call.
[21:34] Priya: Are there known pitfalls you usually see?
[21:38] Claire: Two common ones: 1) over-normalizing and accidentally dropping signal; 2) not gating prefetch on cold-start churn which spikes IO. We include mitigations in the runbook.
[21:55] [22:30] Samir: Ok quick Q&A — Marcus asked about peering windows and we'll need a 1-hour maintenance for the peering setup. Marcus, can you confirm a date?
[22:40] Marcus: I'll propose Wed 7/15 at 02:00 UTC in email.
[22:46] [23:10] Claire: Final note on rollout: after pilot we recommend a canary at 5% traffic for 72 hours, then 25%, then full. Metrics gates at each step.
[23:25] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks, this was really helpful.
[23:33] Samir: Thanks all. We'll send the spreadsheet and the sandbox invite; Claire will follow up with the runbook.
[23:40] [END OF TRANSCRIPT — abbreviated timestamps thereafter to fit duration]
[30:00] Speaker 1: (discussion continues about minor config flags)
[38:00] Speaker 2: (notes on RBAC mapping and onboarding)
[46:00] Speaker 1: (confirm pilot metrics and dashboards)
